summary.description: PAHs are a group of chemicals typically found as crystalline solids that attach to soot particles in the environment. They are not intentionally manufactured but are widespread due to combustion and industrial processes.
emission_sources: Natural sources such as forest fires
environmental_impact: PAHs can cause serious health effects including eye, liver, skin, and immune system damage, as well as genetic damage and cancer
They can be transported long distances through the atmosphere, affecting ecosystems far from the source
Contribute to air and soil pollution, harming wildlife and biodiversity

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: PAHs are linked to severe health effects such as cancer, immune suppression, and organ damage, making them a major concern for public health.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG11_Sustainable_Cities_and_Communities: Urban combustion processes contribute heavily to PAH emissions, degrading air quality and endangering residents' health and urban ecosystems.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG15_Life_on_Land: PAHs can accumulate in soil and harm terrestrial wildlife, with long-term effects on biodiversity and ecosystem resilience, even far from their emission source.
